correctness.rationale: For real cyclic signals with p prime=1(mod4), the difference D maps signals modulo constants isomorphically to H={u:sum u=0}, and the H unit l1 ball is convex hull of (e_i-e_j)/2, so the sharp TV norm of translation-invariant projection is half the maximal l1 norm of difference between shifted convolution kernels. Classical quadratic Gauss sum gives K(0)=(p-1)/(2p), K(x)=(-1+sqrt(p)chi(x))/(2p) otherwise; Legendre autocorrelation sum_x chi(x)chi(x-d)=-1 yields kernel-difference l1=1+(p-1-2chi(d))/(2sqrt(p)), maximized on quadratic nonresidue arc jumps. The exact norm is 1/2+(p+1)/(4sqrt(p)). A small arc perturbation h and real Fourier basepoint with coefficients 2lambda aligned on residues give the EXACT nonlinear difference S_lambda(b+h)-S_lambda(b)=P_R h+mean(h)1 and hence an attained sharp lower witness for BV Lipschitz. Coordinatewise radial proximal nonexpansivity, Fourier commutation with D and Parseval give upper sqrt(p), not an asserted exact nonlinear constant. Independently recomputed kernel shifts for p=5,13,17,29,37 and all nonzero d, agreeing with nonresidue maxima and formula; these finite p calculations corroborate the all-prime arithmetic proof.
